text:
maya: Heads up — dashboards are showing a big client-side stall after the 11:12 deploy. LCP for the heatmap and sparklines jumped ~1.8s on canary. :eyes:

alex: seeing it in RUM too, spikes line up with build 2025.11.12. Can reproduce locally with canary bundle.

sam: any stack traces? main thread decode or GC?

maya: looks like main-thread JS parse/compile and then a long decode for a vendor chunk. Devtools shows a 400–700ms parse for `embedlib.js` on slower pods.

jin: oh right — we added the new `embedlib` lazy-import last week and a small polyfill. Could be chunk boundary change.

maya: exact flame: parse -> compile -> long v8 optimisation pause -> layout. telemetry RUM trace: `73% parse`, `18% compile`, `9% layout`.

alex: sample payload from Sentry RUM: {"url":"/dashboard/overview","bundle":"canary-2025.11.12","chunk":"vendors~embedlib"} — large inline source maps?

sam: are we shipping source maps in prod by mistake? that would blow parse time.

jin: no, source maps are stripped. bundle size delta: +48kb gz after the change. Not huge but the chunk is not async-splittable because of the `export * from './compat'` pattern.

maya: also saw a KV-prefetch miss storm when users jump between routes, which increases concurrent parse. Might be a cache-affinity/thundering effect when prefetch hits bad shard.

ops: logs show many `kvcache.eviction` events at the same times as the RUM spikes. Prefetch policy hit quota and fell back to sync load.

alex: can we temporarily flip prefetch policy to `low` for canary users? That would reduce concurrent network + parse.

jin: yeah we can change a feature-flag in console-config: `prefetch.policy: "low"`. simple rollout.

maya: also a fast revert option: revert the embedlib import to the old dynamic path that splits to smaller chunks. I can open a PR, but flipping prefetch is quicker.

deploy-bot: build 2025.11.12 is currently routed to canary (5%). Next rollout scheduled in 22m.

sam: quick experiment: try `curl -H "x-canary: 1" https://console-proxy/...` + emulate slow CPU in chrome to reproduce. I can test in 10m.

alex: agree flip prefetch first. Jin, can you patch the FF and stage a config change? Put 0% for canary if necessary.

jin: doing it now. patch: ```json
{ "console": { "prefetch": { "policy": "low", "canaryPct": 5 } } }
```

jin: pushed, will propagate in ~2m. ci-bot: ran config check OK.

ci-bot: config-lint: OK. feature-flag change deployed to configstore (version 4321).

maya: canary telemetry starting to look better — LCP median down ~700ms after change. not back to baseline but much improved.

alex: uncleared hypothesis: the `embedlib` chunk still has a hotspot for slower CPUs (ARM dev machines we use for canary). We should split that chunk into two and remove the compat export pattern.

sam: agree, but that's a code change. Plan: 1) keep prefetch low 2) schedule embedlib split PR 3) add a quick integration that runs simulated slow-CPU parse perf on each PR.

jin: noted. I'll open the PR for split and add the test harness entry.

ops: we should also tune kvcache eviction thresholds temporarily to avoid the prefetch->evict cascade. lowering `kvcache.maxEntries` may help.

maya: +1 on eviction tuning. But careful — lowering might increase misses overall. Let's do small adjustments and monitor.

alex: action items — jin flips prefetch (done), jin opens embedlib-split PR, ops experiments small kvcache threshold tweak, sam runs slow-cpu smoke, maya monitors RUM and dashboard metrics.

maya: thanks team. If anyone sees regressions revert the flag to previous version (canaryPct: 5 -> 0) and notify. :thumbsup:

jin: PRs / links: https://git.internal/console/pulls/4212 (embedlib split draft), config change id 4321, deploy audit: https://deploys.internal/2025/11/12/2025.11.12

sam: testing now with CPU slowdown. will post a short gif if I can reproduce.

alex: great. moving this thread to follow-up — will file a short postmortem if embedlib split lands later.

maya: closing loop — prefetch flip helped, leaving patch in for 24h to gather stable metrics.

ops: noted, will watch kvcache and eviction logs overnight.

maya: thanks all.
